note: How a GENERIC material tag is read in each culture. ontology/furniture.json tags a piece with words like 'wood', 'fabric', 'stone' — and materials.ts used to flatten every one of them the same way for all three cultures: wood->cedar, fabric->linen, stone->limestone. The consequence was that a Moroccan sedari (tagged brocade, fabric, cedar, wood) rendered in exactly the same cream linen as a Lebanese sofa, so converting a room to Moroccan changed its data and nothing you could see. A specific tag — velvet, marble, limestone, zellige, leather, brass, walnut — still means itself in every culture and is never routed through here.
rule: Upholstered categories prefer an upholstery material over a wood one, whichever tag came first. A 'Brocade armchair' whose tags happen to list cedar before brocade is still upholstered, and reading it as a plain wooden frame is what made every culture look brown.
